text: The book classifies isolated singularities by the principal part of the Laurent series. An essential singularity at z₀ is the case where the principal part:
choices: has finitely many terms, the lowest being 1/(z − z₀)^m
consists of the single term c₋₁/(z − z₀)
explanation: An essential singularity has a principal part with infinitely many non-zero negative-power terms; by Picard's great theorem f then attains every complex value (with at most one exception) infinitely often in any punctured neighbourhood. A finite principal part ending at 1/(z − z₀)^m is a pole of order m, a vanishing principal part is a removable singularity, and a lone c₋₁/(z − z₀) is a simple pole.
